answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by capping active trading slots and auctioning them each epoch, like berths at a busy wharf: only a fixed number of agents may trade, and each berth goes to the highest bidder for that epoch. A lone honest agent needs one berth, but a farmer wanting a thousand fake voices must outbid honest traders for a thousand berths, so the price of each extra slot climbs as the fake fleet grows. Even a ferrous-strong bankroll bleeds fast when every clone must win its own auction, and the basalt-hard cap means copies cannot simply multiply for free.
